scenes.heading: Journey to Bittergrass Fen
scenes.purpose: Use the hour-long walk to connect the rescue to the campaign objective.
tips: Riffel explains that Teremini serves Soth, her soldiers stole the shard, and the failed warden assault left Valendar captured.
The party can identify the stolen shard as the fifth rod piece. Valendar is the next source of detailed vault information.

scenes.heading: Approaching the Fen
scenes.purpose: Run a rescue under pressure rather than a mandatory kill.
tips: Put the temple door on your scratchpad: AC 20, 225 HP, immunity to poison and psychic damage.
Left alone, the borthak attacks the door each turn. An attack on the borthak draws its attention away from the door.
The seven wardens inside are rescue targets. Argentia later speaks for this group; do not add her as an eighth trapped warden.
watchFor: The underground temple is not drawn on map 6.2. Use its textual description rather than inventing mapped rooms.
next: Distracting the Borthak supplies the rescue timing.

encounters.name: Bittergrass Fen rescue
encounters.trigger: The borthak is attacking the temple door when the party arrives.

creatures.name: Borthak
creatures.note: Initially attacks the temple door unless diverted.

creatures.name: Werewolf
creatures.note: Allies trapped inside: change alignments to neutral good. These are not seven hostile enemies.

tactics: Track the door separately as an object.
Add Riffel only if you want his allied actions in initiative; he is separate from the seven trapped wardens.
encounters.resolution: End the encounter when the borthak is defeated or the party and all wardens have escaped.

scenes.heading: Distracting the Borthak
scenes.purpose: Make the distraction and evacuation happen on visible turns.
tips: Throwing the fruit takes an action: on its next turn the borthak moves to it and spends its action eating.
Holding the fruit within 20 feet instead draws pursuit and attacks. It is not a safe charm effect.
Riffel squeezes under the door while the borthak is occupied. On his next turn, he and the wardens open the door and begin escaping north along the bluff.
watchFor: Do not continue a fight to the death after everyone has escaped merely because the borthak is alive.

scenes.heading: Bittergrass Fen Features
scenes.purpose: Make the terrain useful without adding new mechanics.
tips: A creature within reach can push a floating boulder with an action and DC 15 Athletics; Dispel Magic can also make one fall.
A creature in a falling boulder’s path makes DC 15 Dexterity or takes 2d10 bludgeoning damage.
The bank within 20 feet of the creek’s eastern shore is difficult terrain.

scenes.heading: The Blue Fire Wardens
scenes.purpose: Use Argentia’s debrief to give the party a plan.
tips: Explain that red moonlight turned the wardens’ own transformations against them during the Night of Blue Fire.
Teremini learned the magic and ritual from Orinix; barriers protect her and the components while she concentrates.
Argentia points the party toward rescuing Valendar for a way to stop the ritual, not straight into an unwinnable barrier assault.

scenes.heading: Wardens’ Aid
scenes.purpose: State the help and its limits clearly.
tips: The wardens give the party a Moonbeam scroll. Argentia also explains that Valendar may need to be brought close to death to regain his true form.
For 12 hours, Riffel and allies within 10 feet of him are immune to Forced Transformation. This is not universal immunity to every harmful red mirror effect.
The ward can be cast only once. Riffel needs to bring Valendar back promptly; he is not automatically a permanent dungeon companion.
next: The walk to the vault takes about an hour; Riffel waits outside the secret entrance.

scenes.heading: Environmental Effects
scenes.purpose: Separate the exterior aura from local room effects.
tips: The red moonlight affects the 1-mile area around the vault; the general environmental effects are suppressed in the vault’s locations.
A werewolf exposed to the aura is forced into wolf or hybrid form and poisoned. At 10 HP or fewer it can change shape; Remove Curse suppresses Forced Transformation for 1 hour.
Reduced Gravity halves falling damage and doubles jump distance while that effect applies. Check Moonlight Shifts when the ritual ends rather than assuming the old protections remain.

scenes.heading: Moonlight Mirrors
scenes.purpose: Treat mirrors as fragile tools with specific acquisition conditions.
tips: Each mirror is a Medium object: AC 13, 5 HP, immune to poison, psychic, and radiant damage.
An uncovered reflective face illuminates a 20-foot hemisphere in its moon’s color. Covering it matters, particularly in Valendar’s cell.
There are two mirrors of each color. V31’s logbook lists all six locations; V29 provides the matching solution.

scenes.heading: Vault Locations
tips: Separate player-visible description from GM-only information. Use the complete passage for exact checks, timing, and consequences.

scenes.heading: V1: Entrance
scenes.purpose: Run the sentries and the one-use doorway trap as separate threats.
tips: Two moonlight guardians attack intruders on sight.
Pulling either crescent handle triggers a 30-foot cone for 1 minute. Check entry/start-of-turn saves, not just the initial touch.
The trap’s DC 17 Constitution save deals 5d10 radiant, half on success. A creature outside its true form has disadvantage and reverts on failure; the trap cannot be retriggered.

encounters.name: Secret entrance sentries
encounters.trigger: Intruders are seen at the secret entrance.
tactics: The guardians fight until destroyed; track the doorway trap separately.
encounters.resolution: Defeating the guards does not disarm an untriggered doorway trap.

scenes.heading: V2: Anteroom
scenes.purpose: Offer equipment and a theme of retreat without imposing a new obstacle.
tips: The inscription is Elvish and endorses living to fight another day.
The treasure includes a +1 longsword, shield, breastplate, and Potion of Vitality. The chest is unlocked.

scenes.heading: V3: Escape Tunnel
scenes.purpose: Make the escape passage understandable from each side.
tips: From the north, the glowing runes and their operation are obvious on examination; tracing them briefly removes the wall.
From the south, finding their faint light requires DC 20 Investigation. Both sides can activate the route once the runes are found.

scenes.heading: V4: Halls
scenes.purpose: Use a local alarm, not instantaneous awareness throughout the keep.
tips: Four wraiths patrol here. Guerthel carries the key for V7 and V10.
A wraith uses its action to sound its horn when it sees an intruder or is attacked. Allies in V8 can hear within 100 feet.
A dungeon horn is not audible in the keep above, and vice versa. Add V8 reinforcements only if the alarm actually reaches them.

encounters.name: Dungeon patrol
encounters.trigger: A wraith sees or is attacked by an intruder.

creatures.name: Wraith
creatures.note: Guerthel carries the V7/V10 key.

tactics: Spend an action on the alarm before applying its reinforcement consequences.
encounters.resolution: Track V8 troops as the same individuals if they join; do not spawn a second garrison.

scenes.heading: V5: Scrying Chamber
scenes.purpose: Make Soth’s remote presence dangerous without placing Soth himself here.
tips: Touching the silver liquid alerts Lord Soth with a ping. He can answer through the sphere.
Anything other than deference to his manifested face can bring out a weaker death-knight facsimile.
Use a death knight, not Lord Soth’s appendix block, for the projection. Destroying it also destroys the sphere.

encounters.name: Soth’s silver facsimile
encounters.trigger: The party responds to the manifested face with something other than deference.

creatures.name: Death Knight
creatures.note: A projection made from the sphere; not Lord Soth himself.

tactics: It follows Soth’s directives without requiring his action.
encounters.resolution: If the facsimile is destroyed, the sphere disappears too.

scenes.heading: V6: Empty Cells
scenes.purpose: Use the howling as a lead to the rescue target.
tips: The empty cells are not an additional encounter. Valendar’s howls come through the locked western door.
Guerthel’s key opens V7; thieves’ tools and an action allow a DC 16 Sleight of Hand attempt.

scenes.heading: V7: Valendar’s Cell
scenes.purpose: Rescue a terrified prisoner rather than present a disposable monster.
tips: The red mirror keeps Valendar in hybrid form; he mistakes the party for his tormentors and attacks.
The mirror can be removed without special effort. Do not assume detaching an uncovered mirror stops it emitting moonlight.
At 10 HP or fewer, Valendar reverts to his true form. Track this threshold explicitly instead of reducing him to 0 by default.
Once restored, he explains the crystals and mirrors, then leaves through the escape tunnel to meet Riffel. Asking about his shame reveals his qualifying secret.
watchFor: Valendar suggests the mirror strategy but does not give the exact color solution; the orrery supplies it.
next: V15 can provide another helpful explanation; V29 reveals the combination.

encounters.name: Rescuing Valendar
encounters.trigger: The party opens his cell and he mistakes them for tormentors.

creatures.name: Werewolf
creatures.note: Valendar: chaotic good; rescue target; reverts at 10 HP or fewer.

tactics: Track the mirror’s illuminated area and the 10-HP threshold.
encounters.resolution: Once restored, let the explanation and escape proceed rather than forcing combat to continue.

scenes.heading: V8: Garrison
scenes.purpose: Track the actual garrison, including any troops already moved.
tips: The full roster is sixteen skeletons, nine zombies, and two ogre zombies unless already called away.
If V4’s horn brings these troops into another room, deduct them here. The source does not create replacement soldiers.

encounters.name: Underground garrison
encounters.trigger: The party confronts the troops here or a local alarm calls them into the fight.

creatures.name: Skeleton
creatures.note: Reduce the count if these individuals have already left.

creatures.name: Zombie
creatures.note: Reduce the count if already deployed.

creatures.name: Ogre Zombie
creatures.note: Reduce the count if already deployed.

tactics: Keep reinforcement locations and individual damage consistent across rooms.
encounters.resolution: Update the surviving roster rather than resetting the room.

scenes.heading: V9: Winding Staircase
tips: The spiral stair rises 50 feet to V32. This is a connection between levels, not an additional encounter.

scenes.heading: V10: Trapped Black Rose Bearer
scenes.purpose: Release a contained danger only when the locked room is opened.
tips: Guerthel’s key opens this room; an action with thieves’ tools permits DC 10 Sleight of Hand.
Akaazi locked the raging bearer here. It attacks entrants and fights until destroyed.
The north doorway leads up to V35. The supplied Markdown has a malformed V10 heading; the full room text remains preserved.

encounters.name: Confined black rose bearer
encounters.trigger: Someone enters the locked chamber.
tactics: No additional occupants are specified.
encounters.resolution: The stair connection to V35 remains available.

scenes.heading: V11: Vault Access
scenes.purpose: Guard the vault approach without pre-opening every vault.
tips: Two minotaur skeletons attack intruders on sight and fight until destroyed.
The brown stain by the northern doorway leads toward the mold hazard; keep it separate from the sealed vaults.

encounters.name: Vault access guards
encounters.trigger: Intruders enter the curved hall.
tactics: Use the hall and closed vault doors as described.
encounters.resolution: The V12 doors remain locked after the guards are defeated.

scenes.heading: V12: Treasure Vaults
scenes.purpose: Treat the sub-vaults as distinct discoveries.
tips: Each locked iron door can be picked with DC 18 Sleight of Hand or forced with DC 18 Athletics as an action.
V12a has the one-use fire glyph: DC 17 Investigation to find it, DC 20 Arcana to disable it. Opening it as anyone except Teremini triggers the printed 20-foot-radius blast.
V12b holds a beholder zombie; V12c is empty; V12d holds Valendar’s equipment. Do not put every reward in the first room.
V12a contains 1,900 gp, ten 100-gp gems, and six 250-gp paintings. V12d includes the greater healing potion, Stoneskin scroll, armor, and blue cloak.

encounters.name: V12b guardian
encounters.trigger: The beholder zombie encounters non-Undead other than Akaazi or Teremini.
tactics: Apply its stated recognition exceptions.
encounters.resolution: The other vaults have separate contents and opening conditions.

scenes.heading: V13: Ruined Vault
scenes.purpose: Flag an external hazard reference instead of inventing its mechanics.
tips: Brown mold covers the chamber and is also difficult terrain. The chapter invokes its usual effects without supplying the complete hazard rule.
The rubble slopes 20 feet up to V14. Do not replace the absent mold rules with a guessed save or damage amount.

scenes.heading: V14: Flooded Basement
scenes.purpose: Use the flooded basement as a route choice.
tips: Standing water makes the floor difficult terrain. The collapsed rooms and downward rubble connection to V13 are described in the source.

scenes.heading: V15: Lunar Shrine
scenes.purpose: Give an indifferent guardian a reason to cooperate.
tips: Casivus is not an automatic enemy. Opposition to Teremini, or polite conversation with DC 14 Persuasion, makes the naga friendly.
A friendly Casivus permits taking the white mirror, points toward the orrery, and gives the V16 passphrase: buried is best.
Casivus does not wish to leave the shrine or accompany the party.
next: The orrery is in V29; V16 leads up the white tower.

encounters.name: Casivus, only if a fight develops
encounters.trigger: The source establishes an indifferent guardian and a friendly route, not mandatory combat. Use this only if your table’s actions produce a fight.

creatures.name: Guardian Naga
creatures.note: Casivus; initially indifferent, potentially friendly.

tactics: Do not invent hostility simply because a statblock is available.
encounters.resolution: Cooperation can provide the mirror and essential leads without combat.

scenes.heading: V16: Locked Stairwell
scenes.purpose: Use the known passphrase before asking for brute force.
tips: The Arcane Lock passphrase is buried is best. Teremini, Akaazi, and Casivus know it.
Forcing the door requires an action and DC 24 Athletics. The stairs rise 30 feet to V17.

scenes.heading: V17: White Tower Ruins
scenes.purpose: Show the upward route and the lookout’s possible response.
tips: A ladder reaches V19. If the lookout expects attackers, she can pull that ladder up; check V19 before treating it as permanently available.

scenes.heading: V18: Veteran Camp
scenes.purpose: Distinguish the six guards from the seventh who joins.
tips: Six veterans patrol the rubble slope; a seventh rests in the northern tent and joins a fight.
They defend the keep with their lives. Track anyone who has already left to answer V22’s horn rather than duplicating them.

encounters.name: Veteran camp
encounters.trigger: The camp’s guards defend the keep against the party.

creatures.name: Veteran
creatures.note: Six initially on the slope; the seventh rushes from the tent when combat starts. All lawful evil humans.

tactics: Position the seventh in the tent initially; do not place all seven on the slope without explanation.
encounters.resolution: Reuse this same roster if the turret calls them elsewhere.

scenes.heading: V19: White Tower Lookout
scenes.purpose: Use the lookout’s alarm and ladder rather than adding reinforcements by fiat.
tips: One veteran watches here. Expecting attackers, she pulls up the V17 ladder and sounds her horn.
The spiral stairs continue to V20. Apply the source’s limits on which level can hear an alarm.

encounters.name: White tower lookout
encounters.trigger: The lookout detects or expects attackers.

creatures.name: Veteran
creatures.note: Lawful evil human; carries a hollow goat horn.

tactics: She can deny the ladder and raise the alarm.
encounters.resolution: Track where the horn can actually be heard.

scenes.heading: V20: Ruined Shrine
scenes.purpose: Provide a second white mirror without assuming discovery.
tips: The mirror is under floor tiles in oilcloth: DC 12 Investigation to find it. Removal then needs no special effort.
The southern stairs reach U1.

scenes.heading: V21: Drawbridge
scenes.purpose: Make gate control a coordinated action, not a single switch.
tips: Both levers must be pulled at the same time; raising or lowering takes 1 minute.
The moat is 50 feet deep and filled with cold snowmelt. Do not invent additional saving throws absent a rule you explicitly supply.

scenes.heading: V22: Lookout Turret
scenes.purpose: Start the stated reinforcement clock when the alarm is sounded.
tips: Two veterans watch the turret. If they see or hear an approach, they sound their horns.
Allies from V18 arrive in 5 minutes, not immediately. Record that time and use the surviving V18 roster.

encounters.name: Turret lookouts
encounters.trigger: The guards see or hear the party approaching.

creatures.name: Veteran
creatures.note: Lawful evil humans with horns; V18 allies can arrive after 5 minutes.

tactics: Sound the alarm and track its actual delay.
encounters.resolution: Do not spawn a second set of the V18 veterans.

scenes.heading: V23: Wall Walk
scenes.purpose: Make the wall walk useful for navigation.
tips: The walkway connects the second floors of the moon towers. Courtyard staircases provide access.

scenes.heading: V24: Rookery
scenes.purpose: Do not turn transport creatures into automatic attackers.
tips: The two bone rocs are trained to ferry passengers to a lower rookery.
They attack only if threatened or harmed. The source does not provide a guaranteed taming or commandeering procedure.

encounters.name: Rookery, if provoked
encounters.trigger: A bone roc is threatened or harmed.
tactics: Apply the stated provocation condition.
encounters.resolution: If unprovoked, the scene need not become a fight.

scenes.heading: V25: Courtyard
scenes.purpose: Orient the party and foreshadow the height of the ending.
tips: The courtyard connects the towers, other buildings, and wall stairs.
The moondisk is 100 feet above this space. That height matters when the ritual’s solid surfaces disappear.

scenes.heading: V26: Barrack
scenes.purpose: Allow an empty service room to remain empty.
tips: These are quarters for non-Undead visitors. No occupants, encounter, or treasure are specified here.

scenes.heading: V27: Armory
scenes.purpose: Keep equipment finds distinct from plot components.
tips: The listed weapons, armor, shields, bolts, and Oil of Sharpness are supplies, not extra moonlight mirrors or ritual clues.

scenes.heading: V28: Royal Quarters
scenes.purpose: Make the black mirror accessible without inventing Soth’s presence.
tips: This room is reserved for Soth’s rare visits; it does not say he is here now.
The black mirror on the throne can be removed without special effort.

scenes.heading: V29: Orrery
scenes.purpose: Deliver the puzzle’s source-backed solution when the orrery is studied.
tips: The current relation is red over white, white over black, and black over red.
Translate this explicitly into the actionable solution: red light on the white crystal, white light on the black crystal, black light on the red crystal.
No ability check is specified for studying the model. Removing the V30 mirror stops the orrery moving.
next: V31 lists mirror locations; the crystals are at U1, U2, and U3.

scenes.heading: V30: Red Mirror Stairwell
scenes.purpose: Offer the second red mirror and keep its consequence clear.
tips: The red mirror comes off without special effort. Removing it stops the V29 orrery.
The stair continues upward through the red tower.

scenes.heading: V31: Teremini’s Quarters
scenes.purpose: Use the logbook as a practical recovery clue.
tips: The log lists white mirrors in V15/V20, red in V7/V30, and black in V28/V36.
It records the stolen rod piece and dragon-supplied crystals, but not their present storage locations. Do not make the log disclose more.
The footlocker is a trained mimic that attacks snoopers. The northern stairs reach U2.

encounters.name: Teremini’s footlocker
encounters.trigger: Someone snoops around Teremini’s room.
tactics: Use the published mimic block; the logbook is a separate clue.
encounters.resolution: The log remains readable after the threat is resolved.

scenes.heading: V32: Stairwell
scenes.purpose: Connect the levels without inventing a new scene.
tips: This stairwell links to V9 below.

scenes.heading: V33: Muster Yard
scenes.purpose: Let tremorsense, not ordinary visual camouflage, reveal the ambush.
tips: Two earth elementals are beneath the mud. They rise and attack when their tremorsense detects intruders.
Mud is difficult terrain. The yard is also the keep’s rally point when an alarm is raised.

encounters.name: Muster-yard elementals
encounters.trigger: Their tremorsense detects intruders.
tactics: Use the muddy terrain and the printed detection condition.
encounters.resolution: Track any other defenders rallied here separately.

scenes.heading: V34. Circle of Undeath
scenes.purpose: Present Akaazi’s workshop and its overhead mirror connection.
tips: Akaazi is a neutral evil human necromancer wizard accompanied by one black rose bearer.
Once aware of intruders, she orders the bearer to attack and fights to the death.
Looking upward reveals the black mirror hanging in V36; this is a clue to a reachable component, not an extra mirror.

encounters.name: Akaazi’s ritual chamber
encounters.trigger: Akaazi becomes aware of intruders.

creatures.name: Necromancer Wizard
creatures.note: Akaazi: neutral evil human.

tactics: She commands the bearer and fights to the death for Soth.
encounters.resolution: The V36 mirror remains a separate acquisition problem.

scenes.heading: V35: Temple
scenes.purpose: Keep the quiet temple’s routes and concealed reward available.
tips: The north stairs descend 30 feet to V10; DC 13 Perception can reveal the secret western door to the courtyard.
The altar’s hollow back shelf holds a Wand of Enemy Detection.

scenes.heading: V36: Akaazi’s Quarters
scenes.purpose: Make this black mirror riskier to obtain than the throne’s.
tips: The mirror hangs over a 20-foot drop on three iron chains. DC 15 Sleight of Hand safely detaches it from one chain.
Failure by 5 or more releases it to fall. Do not silently declare all chains detached after one successful check.
V28 offers the other black mirror if this one is lost.

scenes.heading: V37: Aviary
scenes.purpose: Treat the aviary as occupied but not automatically hostile.
tips: Twenty ravens are caged here as messengers. No attack order or reinforcement effect is specified for their squawking.
The eastern stairs rise to U3.

encounters.name: Aviary, only if needed
encounters.trigger: Use individual tracking only if the party’s actions put the captive birds into an encounter; no automatic fight is specified.

creatures.name: Raven
creatures.note: Caged messenger birds, not assigned hostile guards.

tactics: Do not invent an alarm beyond the described noise.
encounters.resolution: Continue toward U3 if the birds are left alone.

scenes.heading: Upper-Level Features
scenes.purpose: Supply the written fallback if the party has missed the puzzle leads.
tips: If the characters still do not know how to stop the ritual, the source allows one to realize that the answer concerns the moons and that V29’s orrery should be examined.
Use that fallback instead of inventing a new NPC, clue, or required skill check.

scenes.heading: Solid Moonlight
scenes.purpose: Apply the barriers consistently and retain the stated exceptions.
tips: Nothing physical or teleporting can pass through solid moonlight; it also blocks ethereal travel, resists all damage, and cannot be dispelled with Dispel Magic.
Sunburst suppresses affected solid moonlight for 10 minutes. The rod-powered ritual is unaffected by Antimagic Field.
A creature outside its true form that starts a turn on solid moonlight makes DC 15 Constitution or is poisoned until its next turn.

scenes.heading: Upper-Level Locations
tips: Separate player-visible description from GM-only information. Use the complete passage for exact checks, timing, and consequences.

scenes.heading: U1: White Lunarium
scenes.purpose: Flag the white barrier’s touch trap before resolving repeated interaction.
tips: Touching the barrier emits a flash in a 30-foot radius: DC 17 Constitution or blinded for 24 hours.
This is distinct from simply shining the correct colored mirror light onto the crystal.

scenes.heading: U2: Red Lunarium
scenes.purpose: Use the dead warden’s fate to reinforce the stakes.
tips: One deathwolf made from a slain warden guards the red lunarium and attacks intruders relentlessly.

encounters.name: Red lunarium deathwolf
encounters.trigger: The deathwolf sees intruders.
tactics: It attacks viciously and does not retreat.
encounters.resolution: The crystal remains protected while Teremini concentrates.

scenes.heading: U3: Black Lunarium
scenes.purpose: Run the black lunarium’s two guards as separate individuals.
tips: Two black rose bearers have orders to defend the room against intruders.

encounters.name: Black lunarium guards
encounters.trigger: Intruders enter the guarded lunarium.
tactics: Track each bearer independently.
encounters.resolution: Guard defeat alone does not end the crystal barrier.

scenes.heading: U4: Moonbridges
scenes.purpose: Keep each character’s position clear before the collapse.
tips: The bridges are solid moonlight. Track who is standing on them and what escape or flight options they have before resolving ritual disruption.

scenes.heading: U5: Moondisk
scenes.purpose: Treat Teremini’s ritual state and combat state separately.
tips: The fifth rod piece floats between Teremini’s hands while she performs the ritual.
Once disrupted, she pockets the rod and attacks, fighting to the death. Recovering it is not automatic just because the barriers vanish.
Use an archmage with Teremini’s stated lawful evil elf identity; do not invent an extra boss phase.

encounters.name: Teremini Nightsedge
encounters.trigger: The ritual is disrupted; she pockets the rod and attacks.

creatures.name: Archmage
creatures.note: Teremini: lawful evil elf; carries the fifth rod piece after disruption.

tactics: Resolve the simultaneous collapse and Orinix’s arrival before assuming everyone remains on the disk.
encounters.resolution: The party must actually recover the fifth rod piece.

scenes.heading: Disrupting the Ritual
scenes.purpose: Make the solution, alternative, and ensuing danger explicit.
tips: The color solution is red light on white, white light on black, and black light on red.
Removing a lunar crystal from its pillar is also a disruption condition, but it still requires overcoming the stated protection; it is not a free reach-through.
Resolve Moonlight Shifts immediately, then Orinix’s arrival. The chaos creates an opportunity to seize the rod while Teremini responds to the dragon.
If the ritual is not thwarted, the source still directs a confrontation with Teremini elsewhere to recover the piece. Do not end the campaign for missing the puzzle.

scenes.heading: Ritual Duration
scenes.purpose: Create urgency without adding a countdown the adventure does not give.
tips: The completion time is deliberately unspecified. The party can retreat and take a long rest if truly necessary.
Do not invent a fixed round limit and present it as a rule from the book.

scenes.heading: Moonlight Shifts
scenes.purpose: Resolve the disappearance of the arena, not just the protective bubbles.
tips: The exterior crimson curtain, crystal barriers, bridges, and moondisk all disappear.
Characters standing on those surfaces fall 100 feet to the courtyard. Check actual locations and abilities before resolving the fall.
The old moonlight environment is gone; do not automatically carry its reduced-gravity protection into the aftermath.

scenes.heading: Orinix Arrives
scenes.purpose: Let the dragon’s priority create an opportunity, not guaranteed safety.
tips: Orinix emerges from the new portal where the disk was and attacks everyone in sight, prioritizing Teremini.
This is an adult lunar dragon, not a red dragon or a homebrew equivalent.
The party may exploit the fight to recover the rod and leave. The source does not require killing Orinix as the victory condition.

encounters.name: Orinix’s arrival
encounters.trigger: Disrupting the ritual opens the portal and brings the dragon into the courtyard battle.

creatures.name: Adult Lunar Dragon
creatures.note: Orinix attacks everyone, foremost Teremini.

tactics: Retain Teremini’s existing tracked individual if she is still present; do not add a fresh copy.
encounters.resolution: The chapter objective is the fifth rod piece, not necessarily the dragon’s death.

scenes.heading: Next Steps
scenes.purpose: Close the chapter at the correct return doorway.
tips: Once the party has the fifth piece, they can return to Sigil through the doorway in the living tree where they first arrived.
Apply the chapter’s advancement to level 16 after retrieving the fifth piece.
Use the next applicable Sanctum visit to debrief what actually happened and orient the next rod search. Do not assume Valendar, Riffel, or Teremini’s fate.

sanctum.title: The Wizards Three in Sigil
sanctum.heading: A New Plan
sanctum.when: Use this immediately after the failed Wish deposits the party in the Sigil sanctum, before they leave for Web’s Edge.
briefing: Open with the surprise arrival and let Alustriel calmly explain where the characters are, why the sanctum exists, and why the situation matters.
Keep the pitch focused on urgency and help: Vecna is threatening the multiverse, the sanctum wizards need allies, and the Rod of Seven Parts is the contingency.
Have the scene feel like a briefing from exhausted but determined allies, not a mystery to be solved from scratch.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: Vecna’s rise, the sanctum’s purpose, and the first rod-piece lead in Web’s Edge.
npcs.wants: To protect innocent lives, steady the party, and keep the response organized and compassionate.
npcs.portrayal: Warm, calm, and responsible; she leads with kindness and practical resolve.
prompts: Let her speak first when the party is disoriented so the scene feels anchored and safe.
Use her to translate the stakes into plain terms without theatricality.
If the players ask for help, have her offer support, research, or preparation that fits the chapter rather than solving later chapters for them.
npcs.guardrail: Do not make her omniscient; she knows the broad threat and the current plan, not future twists the chapter has not revealed.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: Abyssal and demon-lord lore, the wider multiverse, and enough to warn the party where plans are likely to go wrong.
npcs.wants: To back an alliance that serves her interests and to keep the party from acting foolishly.
npcs.portrayal: Sharp, dry, and brilliant; she is useful even when she sounds impatient or amused.
prompts: Give her one cutting observation or warning after Alustriel establishes the stakes.
Let her sound like a strategist who prefers competence over sentiment.
Use her to reinforce planar danger and the cost of underestimating Vecna or his allies.
npcs.guardrail: Stay with the past version of Tasha described in the source; do not advance her into later-character history or add facts the chapter does not supply.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: The false contingency plan, the first rod piece’s location, and how to push the party toward the next objective.
npcs.wants: To keep the characters moving, keep the deception intact, and eventually get the Rod of Seven Parts into Kas’s hands.
npcs.portrayal: Brisk, scholarly, and confident, with the self-assurance of a veteran archmage who already has a next step in mind.
prompts: Have him present the rod as the only practical route to weakening Vecna and make the first destination sound immediate and obvious.
Let his advice be helpful but always gently steering the party where Kas wants them to go.
If the characters probe his story, keep him polished and evasive rather than openly hostile.
npcs.guardrail: This is Kas in disguise. Do not reveal the masquerade before the chapter’s betrayal scene or let him act in a way that breaks cover.

departure: Send the party out through the portal toward Web’s Edge once they are briefed and equipped.
If the characters borrow items or ask for extra research, keep it limited to the source material and the sanctum’s supported help.
End on momentum: the sanctum is a safe home base, but not a place to linger in suspense.
return: When the party comes back with the first piece, let the portal and the rod point them toward the next destination.
Use the sanctum as a place to rest, confirm what they learned, and hear the next planar lead without overexplaining future chapters.
Keep the tone cooperative: the wizards are allies, not quest dispensers.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not name Kas, Miska, or the betrayal out loud unless the table has already uncovered that secret.

sanctum.title: The Astral Sea Lead
sanctum.heading: A Doorway to Space
sanctum.when: Use after the first rod piece when the party returns to Sigil and needs the route to the Astral Sea and Havock.
briefing: Treat this as a planar orientation scene: the party already has the first piece, and the sanctum’s portal responds to it.
Focus the briefing on the Astral Sea, Havock, and the dead-god lead rather than on lore that the chapter does not need yet.
Keep the wizards’ tone practical and slightly breathless, as if the next leg of the hunt must start immediately.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The Astral Sea basics, the sanctum portal’s planar reach, and the broad shape of the rod chase.
npcs.wants: To help the party move quickly and safely toward the second piece.
npcs.portrayal: Patient and supportive, with the composure of someone accustomed to sending heroes into dangerous places.
prompts: Have her summarize the destination without drama and let the characters ask about anything unclear.
Use her to keep the party focused on the next objective rather than on the size of the multiverse in general.
If they need reassurance, give it in a practical, grounded way.
npcs.guardrail: Do not have her invent additional Astral Plane details beyond the chapter’s briefing.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: The difference between a useful lead and a fairy tale, and the risks of space, dead gods, and spelljamming travel.
npcs.wants: To keep the party sharp and skeptical.
npcs.portrayal: A little sardonic, a little delighted by the scale of the problem, and always intellectually alert.
prompts: Let her add one pointed caution about the Astral Sea or spelljammer travel.
Have her sound like the person in the room least impressed by nonsense.
Use her to underline that the party is crossing into an alien environment, not a scenic detour.
npcs.guardrail: Keep her comments grounded in the source; do not turn her into a guide for unrelated cosmology.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: The second-piece lead and the practical claim that the portal opens near the target area.
npcs.wants: To keep the party moving toward the rod and to maintain his false expertise.
npcs.portrayal: Self-assured, efficient, and just a little impatient to get on with the hunt.
prompts: Have him sound certain about the destination and eager to send the party on their way.
Let him treat the next objective as a solvable magical problem, not an open-ended mystery.
Keep his usefulness plausible so the ruse remains believable.
npcs.guardrail: Do not reveal the impersonation here; this is still the masked version of Mordenkainen.

departure: Direct the party through the sanctum portal to the Astral Plane once the briefing ends.
If they linger, let the wizards answer only the chapter-supported questions and then nudge the scene onward.
Keep the sanctum as a staging ground, not a second adventure site.
return: On the way back, let the sanctum function as a place to confirm the second lead and prepare for the next destination.
The portal should feel like a reliable transition point, not a limitless shortcut with extra benefits.
Do not imply the wizards can replace planar travel or solve the shipwreck section for the characters.
sanctum.spoilers: The Astral briefing should not give away later rod-piece locations or any of Kas’s future moves.

sanctum.title: The Mournland and Mount Ironrot
sanctum.heading: An Important Detail
sanctum.when: Use after the second rod piece when the party returns to Sigil to learn how the Mournland and Mount Ironrot complicate the next search.
briefing: Make this briefing feel like tactical planning: the party has a destination, but the wizards know the terrain is treacherous and the rod’s guidance is imprecise.
Center the scene on docents, warforged, and the Mournland’s unreliable magic because those are the source-supported tools and hazards.
Treat the sanctum as the place where the party learns how to work with local magic rather than brute-forcing the search.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The Mournland background, the rod’s imprecise pointing, and the value of a working docent.
npcs.wants: To help the party plan carefully and avoid wasting time among the ruined colossi.
npcs.portrayal: Steady and thoughtful, like a leader who is used to turning ominous intelligence into a workable route.
prompts: Have her explain the problem clearly: the rod points to Mount Ironrot, but not precisely enough to be useful on its own.
Let her support the docent idea as a practical solution, not a magical miracle.
Use her to encourage methodical searching.
npcs.guardrail: Do not expand the Mournland briefing into unrelated lore or hint at outcomes the chapter has not resolved.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: What makes the Mournland dangerous and why magic can be unreliable there.
npcs.wants: To keep the party from assuming the terrain will play fair.
npcs.portrayal: Sharper than Alustriel, with a skeptical edge that is still helpful.
prompts: Let her emphasize the practical consequences of bad navigation and failing magic.
Have her speak like someone who respects obstacles more than bravado.
Use her to warn the party that the plan depends on local conditions, not just the rod.
npcs.guardrail: Do not give her powers or knowledge beyond the chapter’s sanctioned briefing.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: Why the rod needs augmenting and why the docent is the best way to stabilize its divining power.
npcs.wants: To present the party with an actionable route into the Mournland.
npcs.portrayal: Analytical and a little self-satisfied, as though he has already worked out the hard part.
prompts: Have him explain the docent plan with the confidence of a veteran planar traveler.
Keep the advice technical but understandable.
Do not let him wander into secret-identity territory here; the deception still needs to hold.
npcs.guardrail: Do not imply teleportation or divination will work normally in the Mournland; the source says the opposite.

departure: Send the party to the Mount Ironrot portal once they understand the docent strategy.
Let the wizards’ advice feel like planning support, not a map that removes the challenge.
Close on a sense of rough, practical optimism.
return: When the party returns with the third piece, keep the sanctum focused on the next rod lead and the new complications that go with it.
Use the return to confirm that the docent solution worked as intended if the players ask about it.
The sanctum should still feel like a headquarters, not a place where every problem can be solved in advance.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not overstate how precise the rod’s guidance is in the Mournland; the chapter is explicit that the lead is only approximate.

sanctum.title: Barovia and Death House
sanctum.heading: Barovia
sanctum.when: Use after the third rod piece when the party returns to Sigil for the Barovia briefing before entering Death House.
briefing: Keep the tone gothic and cautious: the party is headed to a Domain of Dread, and the sanctum should frame that as a serious and limited-welcome destination.
Focus on the source-supported basics of Barovia, the Mists, and Strahd’s authority; do not expand into unrelated Ravenloft lore.
Let the party leave Sigil with a clear sense that this is a dangerous detour, not a simple next stop.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The broad shape of Barovia, why Death House matters, and the limits of her own research.
npcs.wants: To prepare the party without pretending the sanctum knows more than it does.
npcs.portrayal: Measured and sincere, with a protective concern for the party’s safety.
prompts: Have her say plainly what Sigil’s research can and cannot tell the characters.
Use her to frame Barovia as a place where the ordinary rules of escape do not apply.
Let her be reassuring without downplaying the threat.
npcs.guardrail: Do not invent extra Barovia facts or promise safe movement through the Mists.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: The limits of getting clean answers from a cursed, isolated domain and the danger of treating Strahd lightly.
npcs.wants: To keep the party from romanticizing the horror or assuming they can bully the domain into submission.
npcs.portrayal: Dry, wary, and experienced enough to know when a place is more trouble than it first appears.
prompts: Let her cut through any false bravado with one blunt reminder about the domain’s nature.
Use her to add a note of cold expertise to the briefing.
If the party asks for certainty, have her give only what the chapter source allows.
npcs.guardrail: Do not give her extra knowledge about Barovia beyond the chapter’s sanctioned summary.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: The route to Barovia and the practical value of keeping the Rod of Seven Parts moving.
npcs.wants: To press the party toward Death House and keep the search on schedule.
npcs.portrayal: Focused and brisk, as if he is already one step into the next plan.
prompts: Have him present Barovia as the next unavoidable stop.
Keep his comments practical and unembellished, as though he is trying to make a cursed land sound manageable.
If the characters ask too many questions, let him answer only at the level the chapter supports.
npcs.guardrail: The disguise is still active; do not reveal Kas or let him talk like a different villain.

departure: Once the briefing ends, send the party through the portal into Barovia.
Do not turn the sanctum into a debate chamber; the source points to the village and Death House, not an open-ended consultation.
Keep the exit decisive and a little ominous.
return: If the party comes back after Death House, use the sanctum to acknowledge the horror they survived and orient them toward the next rod piece.
The wizards should sound like allies who are trying to keep the journey moving, not like people who can undo Barovia’s darkness.
Keep the research limited to what the source says Sigil can actually tell them.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not promise a clean escape from the Mists or leak details about Strahd’s later appearance beyond the chapter’s own setup.

sanctum.title: Krynn and the Peylon Tree
sanctum.heading: Knowledge of Krynn
sanctum.when: Use after the fourth rod piece when the party returns to Sigil for the Krynn briefing before reaching the peylon tree and Three Moons Vault.
briefing: Frame Krynn as a war-torn world where dragon politics, old catastrophes, and current conflict all matter to the search.
Keep the discussion on the chapter’s source-supported beats: dragons, the Cataclysm, and the current war. The rod’s guidance is hazy, but neither the characters nor the Wizards Three knows why.
Let the sanctum feel like a planning room that helps the party choose how to investigate, not a place that solves the vault.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The basics of Krynn and the fact that the portal takes the party there to continue the rod hunt.
npcs.wants: To help the party make sense of the world they are about to enter.
npcs.portrayal: Calm and encouraging, with the authority of a wizard who has handled many dangerous planes before.
prompts: Let her summarize the world in clear, usable terms.
Have her keep the team pointed toward the next lead without overpromising.
Use her to make the transition to Krynn feel deliberate and supported.
npcs.guardrail: Do not add unsanctioned Krynn lore or imply the party knows more than the chapter allows.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: How to read a dangerous plane and why hidden agendas matter on Krynn.
npcs.wants: To keep the party alert to manipulation and factional conflict.
npcs.portrayal: Clever, unsentimental, and slightly amused by the idea that anyone thinks war is simple.
prompts: Let her stress that the world is politically and magically messy.
Give her one pointed warning about assuming the first obvious lead is the whole truth.
Use her to reinforce that the party is entering an active conflict zone.
npcs.guardrail: Keep her grounded in the chapter’s knowledge notes and avoid future spoilers about the vault outcome.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: The rod indicates Krynn and a massive tree, but its indication is imprecise. He does not know why.
npcs.wants: To keep the party moving toward the tree to investigate the incomplete lead.
npcs.portrayal: Assured and methodical, as if he has already thought through the next leg of the search.
prompts: Have him acknowledge the ambiguity as a problem to investigate without claiming to know its cause.
Let him sound like the sort of wizard who expects the party to handle complications in the field.
Keep the briefing practical and fast.
npcs.guardrail: Do not reveal the future betrayal, the vault destination, or the cause of the rod’s distorted guidance in this departure briefing.

departure: Send the party through the portal to Krynn once they have the background they need.
If the players ask for more, answer only with the chapter-supported facts about Krynn and the tree.
Keep the handoff brisk so the party feels the pressure of the search.
return: When the party comes back with the fifth piece, the sanctum should feel like a place to recover and redirect, not to linger in the war story.
Use the return to transition cleanly into the next rod hunt and the next world.
Keep the portal as a support structure, not a magical shortcut that trivializes travel.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not spoil the identity or goals of the factions at Three Moons Vault beyond the chapter’s own briefing.

sanctum.title: The Isle of Serpents and the Tomb
sanctum.heading: Isle of Serpents
sanctum.when: Use after the fifth rod piece when the party returns to Sigil for the Greyhawk briefing before the Isle of Serpents and the Tomb of Wayward Souls.
briefing: Present the island as an old scar of Acererak’s violence and treasure-hunting legacy, with the archaeologists already in motion.
Keep the briefing rooted in the source: the archipelago, the island’s reputation, the tomb’s danger, and the fact that the archaeologists have only partial information.
Make the sanctum feel like a strategic stop before a dungeon crawl, not an encyclopedia entry.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The broad history of the Isle of Serpents and the practical value of sending the party to a place where answers are scarce.
npcs.wants: To help the party prepare without blunting the dungeon’s mystery.
npcs.portrayal: Kind and careful, with the demeanor of someone who understands that some places are dangerous even in summary.
prompts: Have her keep the briefing short and useful so the unknowns at the tomb still matter.
Use her to frame the island as dangerous but navigable if the party stays alert.
If asked for more, let her defer to the chapter’s research material.
npcs.guardrail: Do not reveal tomb secrets or give away the archaeologists’ surprises.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: Acererak’s reputation, the difference between rumor and danger, and how to spot an overconfident plan.
npcs.wants: To keep the party from thinking an old tomb is a simple problem.
npcs.portrayal: Dry and incisive, with a knack for puncturing careless confidence.
prompts: Have her treat the island’s legends as a warning sign rather than a history lesson.
Let her call out any assumption that a tomb is automatically straightforward just because the party has done well so far.
Use her to make the archaeologist setup feel alive and uncertain.
npcs.guardrail: Do not have her predict the tomb’s traps or resolve the chapter’s confrontation in advance.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: The portal’s role, the island’s general hazards, and the rod piece’s direction once the party arrives.
npcs.wants: To keep the quest on schedule and get the characters out the door.
npcs.portrayal: Efficient and a touch impatient, like a scholar who believes movement answers more than discussion.
prompts: Use him to transition from research to action.
Let him sound certain about the destination but not omnipotent about the tomb.
Keep the focus on the next step, not on a broad lecture about Greyhawk.
npcs.guardrail: He remains the false Mordenkainen until chapter 9.

departure: Send the party through the portal to the Isle of Serpents after the briefing.
Do not let the sanctum become a replacement for the archaeologists’ camp or the tomb’s exploration.
Keep the scene moving so the island feels like the next expedition, not a pause.
return: When the party comes back after the sixth piece, use the sanctum to re-center the rod hunt and prepare the move to Avernus.
Let the return feel like a clean shift from dungeon aftermath to the next world-level objective.
Keep any additional help within the source’s research and rest possibilities.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not reveal the Tomb of Wayward Souls’ specific guardians or resolutions before the chapter does.

sanctum.title: Avernus and the Red Belvedere
sanctum.heading: Knowledge of Avernus
sanctum.when: Use after the sixth rod piece when the party returns to Sigil for the Avernus briefing before entering the Red Belvedere and Dragon’s Pride.
briefing: Frame Avernus as a dangerous infernal destination where the final rod piece is tied to Tiamat, Windfall, and the casino’s layered security.
Keep the briefing focused on the source-supported notes: infernal travel, the Red Belvedere, the dragon queen’s influence, and the sanctum’s role as a launch point.
Let the party feel the destination is hostile but legible, not random.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: The party is headed for Avernus and will need to navigate a politically dangerous infernal locale.
npcs.wants: To keep the characters prepared and focused on the final rod piece.
npcs.portrayal: Serious but encouraging, as though she understands the cost of the final stretch.
prompts: Have her present the infernal lead as a high-risk, high-stakes mission rather than a shock twist.
Use her to keep the group steady and purpose-driven.
If they ask about Tiamat, stay with the chapter’s summary and avoid extra dragon-lore digressions.
npcs.guardrail: Do not make her resolve the casino or the sanctum within Avernus for the party.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: Demonology, infernal politics, and how to read a dangerous power structure like the one around Tiamat’s sphere of influence.
npcs.wants: To make the party understand that Avernus is not merely another stop but a place with its own brutal incentives.
npcs.portrayal: Sharper and more infernal in tone here, but still controlled and useful.
prompts: Let her sound like someone who understands fiendish leverage and the hazards of greed.
Use her to warn the party about assuming the casino will behave like neutral territory.
Keep the advice grounded in what the source says about the setting.
npcs.guardrail: Do not turn her into an all-purpose guide to the Nine Hells; keep her comments tied to this chapter’s material.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: How to point the party toward the final rod piece and how to keep the deception intact until the betrayal.
npcs.wants: To finish the rod hunt, preserve the false trust, and position the characters for later loss.
npcs.portrayal: Confident, structured, and almost overly helpful in the way false allies often are.
prompts: Have him stress that the final piece is attainable if the party follows the plan.
Let him handle logistics with a practiced air of competence.
Keep his helpfulness suspicious only in retrospect, not obviously villainous now.
npcs.guardrail: Do not have him reveal Kas’s true intentions before the chapter 9 turn.

departure: Send the party to Avernus through the sanctum route once the briefing is done.
Use the scene to establish the infernal destination without padding out the intro.
Do not imply that travel is safe or casual; it is simply the next necessary step.
return: When the party returns from Avernus with the final piece, the sanctum should immediately pivot into the betrayal scene.
The wizards’ role here is to receive the party, not to give them an extended rest before the story turns.
Keep the return tense because the source says the next beat is the reveal, not a long debrief.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not foreshadow the exact nature of Windfall’s sanctum beyond what the chapter briefing supports.

sanctum.title: Kas Reveals Himself
sanctum.heading: Returning from Avernus
sanctum.when: Use when the party comes back with the completed rod and the disguised wizard is still in place, before the betrayal actually lands.
briefing: Run this as a false calm scene: the party thinks they are back among allies, but the source makes clear the villain is buying time.
Let the fake Mordenkainen urge rest and delay while Alustriel and Tasha believe they are handling the final preparations.
Keep the tension subtle until the reveal, because the chapter’s dramatic turn depends on the party feeling the loss of trust.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: That the party has returned with the final rod piece and that the sanctum is still the party’s staging ground.
npcs.wants: To help the characters rest briefly and stay united while the final plan comes together.
npcs.portrayal: Warm and attentive, but a little fatigued from the strain of the campaign.
prompts: Have her welcome the party sincerely and try to keep the mood steady.
Let her be encouraging without realizing the danger at the table yet.
If she is asked for guidance, keep it to the chapter’s known information.
npcs.guardrail: She does not know Kas has already won the immediate deception; do not let her act as if she suspects the betrayal before the source reveals it.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: The characters are back, the rod is whole, and the final steps toward confronting Vecna are close.
npcs.wants: To finish the plan and move on to the confrontation.
npcs.portrayal: Alert, skeptical, and still useful even when she is off-balance.
prompts: Use her to keep the party thinking about the goal, not just the exhaustion of the journey.
Let her feel competent but not omniscient as the betrayal approaches.
Have her help frame the rod as a tool, not a victory.
npcs.guardrail: Do not let her catch the fake wizard in time; the chapter’s reversal needs to land.

npcs.name: Mordenkainen
npcs.knows: That the final rod piece is in hand and that he needs to stall for time before striking.
npcs.wants: To keep the party resting, take possession of the rod, and spring the betrayal when they are least prepared.
npcs.portrayal: Overly brisk, conspiratorially helpful, and just a little too eager for everyone to trust him.
prompts: Have him push rest, reassurance, and the promise that everything is under control.
Let him sound like the person who has finally done the hard thinking for the group.
Do not let him become openly malicious until the reveal itself.
npcs.guardrail: This is still Kas in disguise. Keep the façade intact until the betrayal scene fires.

npcs.name: Malaina van Talstiv
npcs.knows: That something is wrong with the fake wizard and that her unease is justified, even if she has not proved it yet.
npcs.wants: To protect Alustriel and get the party to notice the warning signs.
npcs.portrayal: Solemn, observant, and quietly worried.
prompts: Use her to heighten the feeling that someone in the sanctum is out of step.
If the party asks, let her be honest about her unease without overexplaining the secret.
Keep her concern grounded in the source’s suspicion, not in omniscient certainty.
npcs.guardrail: Do not turn her into a solution engine; she can raise concern, but the source says the proof arrives too late.

departure: If the party rests, that is the moment the betrayal should happen.
If they resist rest, keep the source-supported alternatives available but don’t let the scene drift away from the impending reveal.
End this visit by handing control to the betrayal rather than to the players’ cleanup plans.
return: After the betrayal, the sanctum is a wounded recovery space: Alustriel and Tasha are alive, shaken, and ready to explain what happened.
Use the return to provide the chase lead to Pandesmos and the Chime of Exile warning.
Keep the scene emotionally sharp; this is the moment the allies become fully honest about the real enemy.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not reveal Kas’s true form before the chapter’s reveal sequence; do not let the fake wizard hand the party the truth early.

sanctum.title: Reunion in Sigil
sanctum.heading: Reunion in Sigil
sanctum.when: Use if the party returns to Sigil before the final push into Vecna’s Grasp, and again as the post-victory homecoming tone for the sanctum.
briefing: Treat this as the last structured sanctum briefing: the party can rest, get oriented, and hear the final guidance about Vecna’s Grasp and the demiplanes.
Keep the information centered on what the source says Alustriel and Tasha know, not on guesses about the last battle.
If you use the post-victory version, let the scene resolve into relief and celebration instead of another tactical lecture.

npcs.name: Alustriel Silverhand
npcs.knows: About Vecna’s Grasp, the three unrealities, and how the party can reach the Cave of Shattered Reflection.
npcs.wants: To help the party finish the job and then honor what they have done.
npcs.portrayal: Compassionate, collected, and finally able to speak as a trusted commander again.
prompts: Have her explain the final plan in clear steps when the party returns before the cave.
If the adventure is ending, let her shift into gratitude and celebration rather than more pressure.
Use her to restore the sense that the sanctum is safe after all the chaos.
npcs.guardrail: Do not have her magically solve Vecna’s final defenses or contradict the source’s description of the demiplanes.

npcs.name: Tasha
npcs.knows: The structure of Vecna’s demiplanar unrealities and the practical limits of the final assault.
npcs.wants: To see the plan through and, if the fight is done, to acknowledge a hard-won victory.
npcs.portrayal: Sharper but more openly allied now, with less bite and more focus.
prompts: Let her contribute the final tactical explanation in crisp terms.
Use her to validate the party’s competence without overpraising them into complacency.
If the party has already won, let her sound genuinely relieved.
npcs.guardrail: Stay within the chapter’s briefing about the unrealities and do not imply the party can skip the required steps.

departure: If the party is heading into the final chapter, send them toward Vecna’s Grasp with the teleportation guidance the source supports.
If the story is ending, move directly into the celebration tone instead of looping back to another quest.
Keep the transition clean: this sanctum scene is the last safe harbor before the endgame.
return: On return, the sanctum should feel like the campaign’s homecoming point—either a final war-room or a place to celebrate survival.
Use it to underline that the allies have made it through the worst of the betrayal and can stand together again.
If the party has already finished the adventure, let the sanctum breathe as the place where the victory lands.
sanctum.spoilers: Do not claim the final assault is trivial; the source says the party still has three unrealities and Vecna’s Grasp to dismantle.
